independence_statement: This reading was made from source/SP114_CW_156-5_scans/J156-5-04_156-5_scan032.jpg and independently generated crops only. I read the assigned CONVENTIONS.md and box coordinate TSV. I did not open witnesses, first-reader transcriptions/crops/notes, page.tex, review or comparison records, or another reader's outputs. I used no OCR, recognition library, external research, or TeX compilation. Box kind labels were treated as locators only; readings and states were decided from visible ink.
image_processing: Fresh crops directly from the source JPG, autocontrast, LANCZOS enlargement to 3000 pixels across; primary unrotated crops received modest UnsharpMask radius 1, percent 60, threshold 3. Rotated replacements were generated afresh from the source and resampled, with white padding. No strokes were erased.

boxes.observations: Two dark digits: first has two open rightward lobes and a lower hook (3); second is a single downstroke with a short left entry and foot (1). No deletion.

A, membership mark, F, backslash, open rounded capital; its lower-right upturn is short and lacks a distinct medial horizontal bar, so C/G remains doubtful. Following formula has A, intersection arch, B. Manuscript 31 sits above B and is separate, not a superscript. The line reads est réunion de strates de F; lower descender of réunion is clipped by this box.

The second, uncancelled word has low r/e/s movement and a tall t, consistent with reste. Accent above à, dotted i in voir, and long descender in que are visible. The following baseline reads une.

Baseline shows strat followed by a steep diagonal insertion guide before de. Above the guide is a looped character with an internal horizontal stroke and a lower return, read preferentially as inserted e; capital G remains possible. Top-edge writing belongs to the previous line and is excluded.

A tall rising l-like curve joins a small closed loop; a lower sweeping rightward stroke may be final s. A strong horizontal cancellation runs through the middle. The initial and final contours remain visible but the middle is overrun.

A= and large U union precede B with small circular superscript. One long strike traverses the display. Below the union: B, curved membership with horizontal tongue, F; second line B with angular less-than and separate lower dash, then a narrow vertical capital with two rightward short strokes, preferentially F but A remains doubtful.

Both first-line G forms have clear internal bars and downward right terminals, and primes are distinct. The relation before F' is an open subset curve. Second-line G after membership is likewise barred, but the two rounded capitals in the parenthesis have no clear internal bar and read visually as C'/C. The order sign has a lower parallel stroke. Bottom edge clips the next line, not included.

The initial tall stem belongs to et; on is reduced to a small dot/entry plus long low arch. Two long closed descending loops in gagne are visible, with small a between. Final word has successive low curved strokes and a separate terminal dot.

Viewed original orientation and a 50-degree clockwise rotation. Large U and two tall following strokes lead into low connected ending read Ultra, with the last a compressed. Second word has a long f descender, closed o, low r and crossed final t. Adjacent upright Corollaire heading is outside note scope.

Heading has a separate underline. Baseline after the short Le/La is heavily crossed; tall paired f loops and final t allow a doubtful raffinement. Subdivision is above that strike. A lower interlinear word shows c, tall h, separated low a/c/u/n/e strokes, read chacune; its long curved insertion guide returns before des. The short abbreviation after des has a descending p, compact r-like shoulder and final dot. Also viewed detail crop from [630,650,985,840].

A broad diagonal X crosses the a) passage as confirmed on whole page. Pour has a separate small o and low ur; toute has a tall initial t. Two primes follow both displayed F'' forms. C' on lower line is open at right; the following rounded capital is crossed by the large diagonal, so its possible internal detail is obscured. The relation has angular upper and separate lower strokes. Top-edge suivantes belongs to the preceding heading; lower-edge insertions are handled in following boxes.

Entire excerpt lies inside the large X cancellation. The baseline word after est has its own heavy horizontal crossing and two lower underline strokes; m and x-like diagonals are partly legible, but maximal is retained as doubtful. Above is un plus grand followed by a parenthesis and abbreviation. Pour has a long p descender, and a large order sign and small upper asterisk stand to the right. The top-edge induit C' sur belongs to the previous line and is not repeated.

Long s/u/b/d/i/v/i/s/i/o/n/s sequence crosses the X. At upper right de F qui induisent continues the same line despite the slanted writing. On next line the first capital has internal horizontal G bar and distinct prime; the last has an open curved bowl and short rising lower terminal without clear bar, hence C/G doubt. Final period is dense black. Adjacent b) material at the lower edge is excluded.

Tiny opening parenthesis, tall looped h-shaped letter with right shoulder, a separate dot, a horizontal segment, angular small final glyph, and closing parenthesis. Large X crosses the horizontal and final glyph. The last glyph may be s; dots/dash cannot be fully distinguished from crossing and guide line. This is the end of the interlinear un plus grand insertion.

First word begins with overlapping upright/looped strokes and a deep descending stroke, making initial d/p and the word's state hard to resolve; preference dans. A separate tall looped l, apostrophe, then three connected low strokes read ens. Whole passage is within the large X cancellation although this far-right box contains no crossing line.

Viewed upright, then at 45 and 30 degrees clockwise. Note has a dark asterisk and five rising lines. First starts on then a tall p and compressed remaining letters. Next has a short looped word ending in tall l and a longer r/v/i-like sequence with final angular stroke; these are not safely resolved. Lower three lines clearly show au, a two-stroke subset/equality-like sign, parmi, des subdivisions, d'un, and another such sign before F. The double left-angle mark above/right is separate from the note; nearby main-text F' and G' are excluded.

Viewed unrotated full box at 19:24:25 UTC, clockwise 40-degree full box at 19:24:45 UTC, and a tighter independent rotated detail at 19:27:20 UTC. The marginal lines read les conditions; an individually scribbled a)-like label precedes b) c) d). Sont équivalentes has tall l/t, and impliquent has a long p and single lower underline. Laquelle, subdivision construite and précédemment are distinguishable. A dense word before impliquent appears individually cancelled, possibly et. The final continuation after Mais has compressed overlapping strokes and remains doubtful. A long continuous curved line runs through interior letters across several lines; deletion is preferred but a grouping/attention mark remains possible, so the entire note has uncertain state. Upright main-text formulas and the top fragment of the preceding marginal note are outside this target.

A small a) stands above the main line, while b) survives at left. Application has two long p stems and a clear looped t; can. is compact followed by dot. The order comparison has clear F prime at left and unprimed F at right. Phi has a closed upper loop and long descender; mapping runs from F' to F with right arrowhead. Bottom-left induit is partly clipped by this crop and read with doubt from the already inspected whole-page view. Adjacent N.B. annotation is excluded.

The drawing beside N.B. is a single long near-vertical black stroke left of all three note lines. It undulates slightly, swells right near the bottom, and ends with a short leftward hook. No arrowhead, closed loop, or crossing through note letters is present. Neighbouring N.B. text is separately transcribed in b20.

The large initial O of On reaches upward to the heading underline, but no stroke crosses On as a cancellation. Va, long descending p of prouver, and p. ex at the right are uncrossed. The source and target of this inserted arrow were both inspected.

boxes.observations: Independently viewed the saved b31 crop in original orientation. The long dark line starts through the conditions line near original x172,y1435, descends with a leftward bow through the middle of the marginal note, then continues through lower note lines and ends in a short upward-right hook near x220,y1920. It is one continuous curved stroke, not part of a letter and not a second diagonal of the main X. It intersects words rather than remaining in blank margin, which favours cancellation; its bracket-like outline leaves grouping possible. The reading therefore preserves both whole-note states, with deletion preferred, and separately reproduces the curve schematically. Text was checked in the same source area and independent b17 detail; adjoining main text is excluded.
